record.ROLE_TEXT:
An established regenerative medicine company with a commercial wound care portfolio and a biologic advancing through FDA licensure. The SVP, Quality Systems will lead the entire quality organization, owning commercial manufacturing quality and a major remediation program for the biologic manufacturing operation. This is a rebuilding role: finalize the remediation plan, restructure and grow the team, and strengthen the quality system with lean resources at first. A rare chance for a seasoned biologics quality leader to make a visible, company-defining impact, with a path for upward mobility.
 
 
**You'll Love This Opportunity Because**

* Two substantial mandates at once: lead biologic remediation through licensure and oversee complex commercial manufacturing.
* Direct exposure to the executive team and board, reporting to a COO who gives department heads real independence.
* A technology- and patient-focused culture at an established leader in regenerative medicine.

**The Ideal Candidate Will Have**

* Senior biologics or biopharma quality executive who has brought a product through BLA and led commercial product quality.
* Has led a company through a pre-license inspection, warning letter, or comparable remediation, with strong FDA working relationships.
* A culture builder who can rebuild a team and deliver with lean resources, not someone looking for a steady-state role.
* Based in Greater Boston and ready to be on site every day.
* Cell therapy experience is a plus but not required.

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking a Senior Manager, Global Development Quality Assurance to join our Global Development Quality Assurance (GDQA) team, supporting our Global Development (GD) organization. In this role, you will lead quality auditing programs, and compliance oversight across GLP activities while collaborating with GD, cross-functional stakeholders, and quality partners. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.
 
 
**When & Where**
Location: Tarrytown, NY
 
 
Work model: On-Site
 
 
**Discover Your Role**

* Responsible for performing QAU functions: Study Audits and Facility/Process audits.
* Audit responsibilities may include external audits conducted globally.
* This role may require 20 – 30% travel (both domestic and international).
* Represent the GDQA department by providing audit and compliance input in cross functional meetings
* Lead the identification of internal quality/compliance issues and act as a catalyst for process improvements to promote standardization and best practices both within GDQA and across Regeneron.
* Represents GDQA on high-priority teams, compliance projects and initiatives both within and across functional areas or other departments as applicable.
* Interpret and may assist in developing policies and standards, and evaluate potentially critical problems not covered by policies, standards, and regulations.
* Provides education and/or training to GDQA and other relevant Global Development departments.
* May participate in regulatory inspections by acting as part of the control and/or inspection room team

**This Role Requires**

* Bachelor’s degree (Master’s degree preferred) with 8+ years of relevant industry experience
* 5+ years in Quality Assurance or a related regulated quality laboratory role supporting bioanalytical, pharmacokinetics and pathology portions of studies
* Prior exposure to Quality in GLP environments required; experience performing QAU functions; GCP exposure a plus
* Expertise with 21 CFR Part 58 (FDA GLP) and OECD Principles of GLP required
* Exposure to ICH E6 (GCP) and CLIA regulations are a plus but not required
* Experience with FDA or other Regulatory Agency Inspections, Sponsors or CROs.
* Systems experience working in LIMS, ELN, Veeva QMS is highly preferred
* Demonstrated skills in taking initiative and working independently in a dynamic environment to effectively manage multiple complex priorities
* Strong leadership with demonstrated ability to interface with both peers and senior leaders
* Critical thinking and problem solving, written and verbal communication skills
* Strong track record of project management, stakeholder management, collaboration skills and negotiation of complex situations
* Attention to detail and accuracy of work

**About LeonaBio:**
LeonaBio, Inc., headquartered in the Seattle, Washington area, is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for high unmet medical needs, including treatment-resistant metastatic breast cancer and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Our lead programs, lasofoxifene and brelgometon, are novel small-molecule therapies with the potential to address devastating diseases where current treatment options are limited or ineffective. We are committed to scientific excellence and patient-centered innovation as we advance meaningful new therapies for patients.
 
 
**Position Summary**
LeonaBio is seeking an experienced, hands-on Vice President, Quality to lead the company's Quality function through the transition from late-stage clinical development to regulatory approval, commercial launch, and lifecycle management. This executive will be responsible for designing, implementing, and scaling a phase-appropriate Quality Management System and Quality Risk Management framework that meets global regulatory requirements, reflects the company's size and stage, and supports commercial operations.
 
 
The ideal candidate has direct leadership experience in a biotechnology company developing and commercializing small-molecule products, with a demonstrated track record of building or materially transforming Quality systems and governance. This individual will integrate product quality, patient, compliance, supply, vendor, inspection, and commercialization risks into enterprise decision-making and provide clear, risk-based guidance to executive leadership and the Board. The Vice President, Quality will foster a practical culture of quality that supports timely business decisions, inspection readiness, reliable product supply, and sustainable commercial operations.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Serve as the executive leader for LeonaBio's Quality function, providing strategic direction across quality systems, clinical development, manufacturing, and regulatory compliance.
* Develop and execute a scalable, phase-appropriate Quality strategy that supports late-stage clinical development, regulatory submissions, commercial readiness, and lifecycle management.
* Own the architecture, implementation, effectiveness, and scaling of the company's pharmaceutical Quality Management System (QMS) and Quality Risk Management (QRM) framework, ensuring inspection readiness and alignment with a lean, outsourced operating model.
* Ensure compliance with applicable global GxP requirements, including GMP, GCP, and GVP, while maintaining a pragmatic, risk-based approach to Quality. Lead inspection readiness, audits, quality governance, and timely resolution of observations.
* Establish and oversee the Quality governance model for CMOs, CDMOs, CROs, contract laboratories, suppliers, and other GxP partners, including qualification, quality agreements, audits, performance monitoring, risk escalation, change control, investigations, validation, and supply continuity.
* Provide Quality leadership across small-molecule drug substance and drug product development, technology transfer, process validation and PPQ, analytical methods, stability, specifications, packaging, commercial launch, and post-approval lifecycle management.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality organization, including leadership of the Senior Director of Quality Assurance, while fostering accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree (MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive Quality experience in biotechnology or pharmaceutical companies, including significant leadership responsibility in lean, resource-constrained environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality strategy through late-stage clinical development, regulatory submissions, and commercial readiness, including first product launches, with direct sma

Overview:

Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.

With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

The Cancer Epidemiology Program, as one of five scientific programs within the Public Health Sciences Division, is focused on reducing cancer incidence, progression, mortality, and sequalae through the identification of risk (or protective) factors, the elucidation of underlying biologic mechanisms, and the translation of discoveries into prevention strategies. The program includes more than a dozen core faculty based at Fred Hutch, plus affiliated faculty from the University of Washington, as well as a large number of research staff, ranging from program assistants, interviewers, medical record abstractors, project coordinators, study managers, and statistical research associates.

Signia Aerospace is a global, integrated provider of high-performance systems and specialized components for the aerospace industry. The Signia brands are leaders in their respective markets and provide a compelling value proposition to both aerospace and defense OEMs and end-users.
 
 
**Position Overview**
Onboard Systems Hoist & Winch, located in Anaheim, CA is one of the world’s leading providers of Search & Rescue (SAR) and Human External Cargo (HEC) advanced mission equipment for civil, commercial, and military helicopters.
 
 
The Director of Quality is a key leadership position reporting directly to the General Manager (GM), responsible for establishing and executing the company's overall quality strategy. This role provides strategic direction and oversight of the Quality function, ensuring the effectiveness of the Quality Management System (QMS), compliance with AS9100 and applicable regulatory and customer requirements, and continuous improvement across all business operations. As the designated FAA Part 145 Accountable Manager, the Director has authority over all Part 145 repair-station operations, ensures personnel follow applicable FAA regulations, and serves as the primary contact with the FAA. The Director also partners with executive and operational leadership to drive quality performance, manage organizational risk, and foster a company-wide culture of quality and accountability.
 
 
**Location:**
Anaheim, CA (on-site)
 
 
**Schedule:**
Monday - Friday
 
 
**Pay:**
$180,000 - $225,000, plus bonus eligibility
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Quality Management System Leadership
* Establish quality strategy, policies, and measurable objectives aligned with the company's business goals.
* Own and administer the company-wide Quality Management System in accordance with AS9100 (which incorporates ISO 9001) and applicable customer and regulatory requirements, including FAA and, where applicable, EASA requirements.
* Oversee the FAA Part 145 repair-station quality control system, including the Repair Station Manual, Quality Control Manual, Operations Specifications, and documented inspection and return-to-service controls.
* Ensure the QMS is effective, scalable, consistently deployed across the business, and aligned with the company's growth and product roadmap
* Lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives to optimize quality processes, procedures, documentation, and controls.
* Manage document control and maintain accurate, controlled quality procedures, process documentation, and compliance records.
* Compliance & Customer Support
* Serve as the primary point of contact for external audits, including AS9100 certification audits, customer audits, and regulatory assessments.
* Prepare the organization for audits and lead audit responses, corrective actions, and follow-up activities to verify effective closure.
* Build and maintain credibility and trust with executive stakeholders, aerospace OEM customers, auditors, regulatory officials, and relevant industry partners.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable standards, customer requirements, and contractual quality clauses.

* Support Manufacturing, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams with timely quality guidance and issue resolution.
* Establish quality KPIs and targets, monitor trends, and report performance and improvement plans to t

**About Us**

At Team Housing Solutions, we deliver exceptional temporary lodging services to organizations deploying teams across the United States and globally. We build flexible, on-demand housing solutions by partnering with property owners, asset managers, and third-party providers, driving cost efficiency and operational agility for our clients.

Our mission is to provide superior temporary lodging experiences through streamlined systems, impeccable service, and a collaborative spirit that values our dedicated team, supply partners, and clients alike.

**About the Role**

The Deputy Director of Site Operations is the leader of a dynamic, multifunctional team delivering temporary support facilities to government and private entities for law enforcement, security, undocumented immigrants, emergency evacuations, energy sector workers, and all Team Housing Solutions (THS) clients. The Deputy Director of Site Operations is responsible for ensuring the THS facilities meet THS, industry standards, and client expectations for a comfortable “home away from home” for all THS clients utilizing THS facilities service members and ensuring that the THS facilities are maintained and operating at the highest levels of service. The Deputy Director of Site Operations has a wide range of responsibilities, from financial planning to staff management and client satisfaction. This position requires frequent and significant nationwide travel to THS facilities (including multiple days working at remote facilities for up to 70% of the time), a high level of organizational skills, agility, strong mastery of leadership competencies, and personnel management skills.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide management oversight of THS facilities’ leadership team in a meticulous manner to maintain THS high-quality standards.

* Be on-site at the facilities on a regular basis to observe operations and implement improvements.
* In coordination with THS’ HR and leadership, the Deputy Director of Site Operations will recruit, train, develop, and manage each facility team to ensure the client is highly satisfied with THS’ performance levels.
* Establish relationships with clients and obtain regular feedback to ensure high satisfaction levels.
* Ensure compliance with health and safety regulations, industry standards, permitting, and licensing requirements for each facility.
* Develop and implement operational policies and procedures for each facility, including but not limited to logistics, safety, and procurement procedures.
* Address client complaints and ensure client satisfaction through effective problem-solving.
* Identify high-performing employees and see them through professional growth within THS.
* Manage, document, and implement action expeditiously to address the underperformance of direct reports in coordination with leadership and Human Resources to support the business’ needs.
* Regular communication with the VP of Construction & Sustainment to provide updates on the status of operations at each facility. Become a trusted advisor to the VP of Construction & Sustainment by full managing the daily details of all the field facilities, enabling the VP of Construction & Sustainment to develop the operational strategy more effectively.
* Be the link between THS leadership and facilities personnel as a leader, analytical person, and decision maker to improve processes and service quality.
* In coordination with THS leadership, the Deputy Director of Site Operations will interface with Government personnel to address the client’s mission requirements.
* Develop and oversee the implementation of work standards, prepare personnel and project schedules, review work discrepancies, and communicate Government policies, purposes,

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Summary**

The Sr. Director of Oncology Operations at Arizona Center for Cancer Care (AZCCC) provides operational leadership and oversight for outpatient oncology operations across AZCCC and its health system partner’s integrated cancer care network. This role oversees strategy, operations, and continuous improvement for infusion centers, physician practices, and outpatient clinics, as well as leadership of the oncology research and clinical trials program. The Director partners with physicians, clinical teams, and research leaders to optimize access, quality, and patient outcomes.

**Duties and responsibilities**

* Provides executive leadership and oversight for all outpatient oncology operations across AZCCC and its health system partner’s integrated cancer care network, including infusion centers, physician practices, and hospital outpatient department (HOPD) clinics.
* Drives the strategic alignment and execution of oncology services to ensure high-quality, efficient, and patient-centered care.
* Oversees the oncology research and clinical trials program, including compliance with NCI guidelines, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable regulatory requirements.
* Collaborates with physician leadership and the Executive Medical Oncology Committee to develop and implement operational strategies that improve access, outcomes, and overall performance.
* Partners with physician investigators and research teams to integrate clinical research with patient care, supporting innovation and advancement in oncology treatments.
* Provides direct supervision and mentorship to clinic operations leaders, including practice administrators and department managers, ensuring operational goals are met across all sites.
* Monitors financial performance, develops annual budgets, and implements cost-control measures while maintaining high standards of quality and service.
* Ensures compliance with AZCCC policies, state and federal regulations, and accreditation standards across all outpatient oncology programs.
* Fosters a collaborative and accountable culture by promoting communication, transparency, and professional growth across interdisciplinary teams.
* Leads initiatives to optimize workflows, staffing models, and patient flow to achieve operational excellence and improve the patient experience.
* Serves as the primary liaison between senior leadership, physicians, and partner organizations, ensuring alignment of goals and strategies across entities.
* Uses data-driven insights to evaluate program performance and identify opportunities for growth, efficiency, and innovation
* Represents AZCCC and performs other related duties as assigned to support organizational goals and promote best practices in oncology care delivery.

**Licensure and Certifications**

* NA

**Direct Reports**

* Regional Practice Administrators

**Qualifications/Education Requirements**

* Master’s degree in health administration, business administration, or a related field required.
* Equivalent combination of education and progressive leadership experience in outpatient medical oncology operations preferred.
* Ability to demonstrate knowledge of oncology operations, including infusion services, physician practice management, HOPD operations, and compliance with NCI guidelines and GCP standards.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressive leadership experience in outpatient medical oncology operations.

**Working conditions**

* Works in an office or clinical setting.
* Exposed to moderate noise levels.
* Emphasizes collaboration with various stakeholders.
* Necessitates effective communication and teamwork.
* Functions in a fast-paced environment.
* May require flexibility in working hours.
* Requires adherence to safety protocols and compliance with healthcare regulations.
* Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between locations.

**Physical requirements**

* Must be able to lift 25 lbs.
* Must be able to sit, stand and walk for extend

Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (Qcells USA), headquartered in Houston, TX, specializes in providing utility-scale modules, solar photovoltaic (PV), and battery energy storage systems (BESS) project development, along with Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) services for solar and BESS projects nationwide. Qcells USA delivers comprehensive turnkey solutions encompassing the entire utility-scale project lifecycle. By choosing Qcells USA for turnkey solutions, customers can reduce uncertainty and risk, leading to enhanced investment returns and contributing to a more sustainable future.
 
 
Qcells USA’s complete turnkey solutions seamlessly integrate the expertise of our Development, Module, and EPC teams, while ensuring close coordination with other vital internal groups such as Project Finance, Systems Integration, and Legal. This collaborative approach ensures that Qcells USA projects deliver exceptional value and performance. With several multi-billion-dollar investments, Qcells is pioneering the establishment of the only complete module supply chain in the U.S., including the expansion of our Georgia module manufacturing facility, which stands as the largest in the Western Hemisphere.
 
 
As an integral part of the global Qcells brand, Qcells USA benefits from a legacy of excellence in photovoltaic manufacturing. Qcells is renowned worldwide for its high-performance, superior-quality solar cells and modules. With dual headquarters in Seoul, South Korea (Global Executive HQ) and Thalheim, Germany (Technology & Innovation HQ), Qcells operates under the umbrella of Hanwha Group, a FORTUNE Global 500 company and one of the top 8 business conglomerates in South Korea.
 
 
**Summary**
The SVP, Environment, Safety, Health & Quality (ESHQ) provides senior executive leadership over all environmental, safety, health, and quality programs across Qcells USA's EPC construction operations. This role is accountable for developing and executing the company's integrated ESHQ strategy, driving a zero-incident safety culture, embedding construction quality excellence into every phase of project delivery, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing ESHQ performance across active utility-scale solar PV and BESS project sites nationwide.
 
 
Working in close partnership with EPC project leadership, site teams, subcontractors, and corporate stakeholders, the SVP, ESHQ sets the enterprise standard for environmental stewardship, occupational health, construction safety, and quality management. This role serves as the primary ESHQ authority for the EPC business, owns the company's Quality Management System (QMS), and represents Qcells USA with regulatory agencies, clients, certification bodies, and industry organizations. This position reports to the COO, or another management personnel that the CEO of the Company may designate. This position is hybrid, based out of our Houston, TX office, requiring up to 4 days per week in the office. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00am to 5:00pm or 9:00am to 6:00pm local time. This position is expected to travel up to 40%.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Define and lead the integrated ESHQ strategy for Qcells USA's EPC business, aligning programs with corporate goals, project requirements, client expectations, and regulatory standards across the ESH and Quality functions
* Build, develop, and manage a high-performing ESHQ organization including site safety managers, environmental coordinators, industrial

As a fabless semiconductor company, the role spans the entire product lifecycle—from architecture through field performance—while driving excellence across external wafer fabrication, assembly and test partners.
 
 
Mission
 
 
Build a world-class Product & Quality Excellence organization that embeds quality into every engineering decision, every supplier relationship and every customer experience.
 
 
Executive Mandate
 
 

* Create an enterprise-wide Quality First culture where quality is designed into products rather than inspected into them.
* Own end-to-end product quality, reliability engineering, supplier quality, customer quality and quality systems.
* Partner with Engineering to strengthen Design for Quality, verification, failure analysis and reliability methodologies.
* Lead quality across outsourced manufacturing partners, ensuring robust process controls, change management and continuous improvement.
* Establish executive quality governance, enterprise KPIs and Board-level reporting.

First-Year Transformation Priorities
 
 
**First 90 Days:**
Assess product quality, reliability, supplier performance, customer escalations, organizational capability and quality systems. Build executive alignment and establish the transformation roadmap.

Launch Design for Quality, supplier excellence and customer quality initiatives. Implement enterprise dashboards, governance and standardized quality reviews.
 
 
**180–365 Days:**
Deliver measurable improvements in field reliability, manufacturing quality, supplier performance, customer satisfaction and organizational quality maturity while building a sustainable culture of continuous improvement.
 
 
Measures of Success
 
 

* Reduced field failures and customer returns
* Improved product reliability and qualification effectiveness
* Higher supplier quality and manufacturing yields
* Reduced Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ)
* Faster root cause analysis and corrective actions
* Improved customer satisfaction and strategic account confidence
* Enterprise adoption of a Quality First mindset

Ideal Executive Profile
 
 

* 20+ years of semiconductor industry leadership with significant experience in analog, mixed-signal or power semiconductors.
* Executive leadership in product quality, reliability engineering, supplier quality and customer quality.
* Experience operating within a fabless semiconductor model using external manufacturing partners.
* Demonstrated success leading enterprise transformation and influencing executive leadership and Boards.
* Technical depth combined with strategic business acumen and exceptional leadership.

Leadership Competencies
 
 

* Enterprise leadership and systems thinking
* Strategic quality transformation
* Engineering partnership and technical credibility
* Customer obsession
* Data-driven decision making
* Global influence without authority
* Talent development and succession planning
* Executive communication and Board presence

Power Integrations is committed to building teams that drive innovation and therefore review a range of factors when determining compensation.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences.
 
 
The Director, Segment Quality Engineering is a strategic technology leader responsible for advancing quality engineering practices across a defined portion of Humana’s technology portfolio. Reporting to the AVP, Quality Engineering – Segment, this role will lead teams responsible for delivery quality, test automation, release readiness, and continuous improvement across multiple product and application teams.
 
 
This leader will work closely with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Platform, DevOps, and enterprise quality partners to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle and improve release confidence, delivery speed, and production stability.

**Responsibilities**

 

* Lead quality engineering strategy and execution across a defined portfolio, domain, or segment.
* Lead and develop quality engineering managers, leads, engineers, and SDETs; drive organization design, talent growth, and team performance.
* Establish portfolio quality goals, KPIs, and governance to improve delivery quality, release readiness, and production stability.
* Embed built-in quality across planning, design, development, testing, and deployment.
* Oversee test strategy and execution across functional, integration, end-to-end, regression, and release validation.
* Own portfolio-level quality risk management, including defect trends, release concerns, environment issues, and cross-team dependencies.
* Drive automation-first practices and integrate quality signals, validation, and gates into CI/CD pipelines.
* Lead adoption of AI-enabled quality engineering capabilities and promote innovative practices that improve speed, coverage, and reliability.
* Sponsor modernization of quality frameworks, tooling, and test approaches for APIs, distributed systems, and cloud-native platforms.
* Oversee non-functional quality practices, including performance, resiliency, operational readiness, and security validation.
* Use metrics and production insights to drive continuous improvement, maturity, and investment priorities.
* Partner with segment and enterprise stakeholders to align execution with broader quality engineering strategy, standards, and reference architecture direction.
* Ensure responsible adoption of AI and compliance with applicable security, privacy, regulatory, and operational standards.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of experience in software engineering, quality engineering, testing, or related technical disciplines.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing quality engineering, test automation, or software delivery teams in large enterprise environments.
* Experience leading quality engineering execution across multiple agile teams or a complex application/product portfolio.
* Demonstrated success driving quality engineering modernization, including automation, tooling, process improvement, and metrics-driven execution.
* Strong understanding of Agile, DevOps, and CI/CD practices.
* Experience with API, UI, integration, regression, and end-to-end testing approaches.
* Familiarity with distributed systems and modern application architectures.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional leaders.
* Experience working in matrixed organizations and leading geographically distributed teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Experience in healthcare or another highly regulated industry.
* Familiarity with member, provider, digital experience, or enterprise platform domains.
* Experience with enterprise quality tools, test management platforms, and engineering lifecycle tools.

**Join Our Team as the Director of Operations at ARRO Water Services!**

This position is responsible for providing strategic leadership and oversight of water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas. The Director of Operations ensures the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of services while maintaining regulatory compliance, operational excellence, and client satisfaction.

The Director of Operations works closely with executive leadership, operations management, regulatory agencies, and clients to support organizational growth, financial performance, and long-term operational planning.

This role is instrumental in developing high-performing teams and fostering a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Essential Job Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas.
* Oversee treatment facilities, pumping stations, distribution systems, and collection systems.
* Ensure compliance with applicable local, state, and federal environmental, safety, and public health regulations.
* Lead, mentor, and develop operations management teams while supporting workforce planning and succession development.
* Develop and implement operational strategies, policies, procedures, and performance standards.
* Oversee operating and capital budgets, financial performance, and resource allocation.
* Monitor operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reliability, and service delivery.
* Establish and maintain strong relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, and key stakeholders.
* Provide leadership during emergencies, system failures, and regulatory incidents.
* Collaborate with internal teams to support infrastructure improvements, asset management, and long-term planning.
* Promote a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with organizational safety policies and OSHA requirements.
* Support business development, client retention, and organizational growth initiatives.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* High school diploma or equivalent required.
* Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Public Administration, or a related field strongly preferred.
* Equivalent combinations of education, certifications, and relevant industry experience may be considered.
* 10–15 years of progressive water and/or wastewater operations experience, including significant leadership experience.
* Pennsylvania Water and/or Wastewater Operator Certification of the appropriate class and subclass required; advanced certifications preferred.
* Valid Pennsylvania driver’s license required.
* Extensive knowledge of water and wastewater treatment processes, PA DEP regulations, and environmental compliance requirements.
* Demonstrated experience managing teams, budgets, and complex operational activities.
* Strong leadership, communication, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills.
* Knowledge of SCADA systems, asset management, and operational technologies.
* Ability to travel regularly between facilities and respond to operational emergencies as needed.

**Benefits**

ARRO Water Services offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, paid holidays, life and disability insurance, and opportunities for professional development, training, and career advancement.

**Daily Work Location/Hours**

This is a full-time, salaried exempt position responsible for overseeing water and wastewater operations across multiple facilities and service areas. Work is performed in both office and field environments, with regular travel to operational facilities, client locations, and meetings.

record.EMPLOYER_PRIMARY_BUSINESS:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Frontier Systems (AFS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized hardware and software products for defense, law enforcement, and intelligence customers. We work alongside our customers to understand their requirements and deliver exquisite capabilities across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements.

Product Operations is the team accountable for the health of the systems and technology that delivers the capabilities that our customers depend on. The function identifies, triages, and drives resolution of incidents across the deployed fleet, and converts what we've learned into the reliability and sustainment insights that product and engineering teams act upon. We work in close coordination with product engineering, reliability, quality, program management, and field operations teams to maximize capability availability for our end users and inform the next cycle of iterations.

 ABOUT THE ROLE

 As the Senior Manager of Product Operations for Frontier Systems, you will own product operations across the division's product portfolio and the programs that deliver those products. You will lead multiple Product Operations managers, each of whom runs a team of technical specialists and engineers focused on supporting and improving fielded products. The division's portfolio is scaling, and this role exists to scale support alongside it, both for the products the function covers today and for the ones that reach the field next.

This is a function maturation and growth role as much as an operating one, and the work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic systems, and the judgment to make decisions whose impact reaches beyond your own team and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 Lead and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Frontier Systems portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also maturing the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people in it.

 Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and to internal Anduril teams. Understand the work at every level, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.

 Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.

 Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning for the function and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.

 Own the Failure Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop: Own the workflow that converts field failures into structured, trustworthy signal for product and reliability engineering, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Partner with engineering to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your own organization accountable to its fidelity.

 Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Mature the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.

 Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes. 

 Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.

 Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.

 Travel and Availability: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations, and to work non-standard hours when fielded operations require it.

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains).

 Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support).

 Organizational Leadership: Experience leading managers and multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program.

 Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.

 Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.

 Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.

 Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.

 Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning for a function and stating the assumptions behind the model.

 Program Management: Project and program management ability applied outside a project management role: decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions.

 Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.

 Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.

 Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

 
 Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.

 Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading air defense, intelligence, and/or force protection teams.

 Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management disciplines (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).

 Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.

 Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.

 Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded robotic and sensor systems, including actuation, power systems, sensing, embedded compute, radar, RF detection, and electro-optical and infrared sensing, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.

 Comfort reading logs, telemetry, and test data, including hands-on use of Linux command-line interfaces and tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, Git, SQL, and Palantir Foundry.

 Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.

 Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.

 Experience in on-call support operations and limited risk tolerance environments.

 An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.

**DIRECTOR OF FABRICATION** 
Sargent Electric is a leading specialty contractor focused on electrical, instrumentation, wireless, utility, and low voltage systems. Founded in Pittsburgh in 1907, we operate from 8 locations across the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast, delivering projects nationwide for our strategic customers. 
We support the breadth of client needs — from routine 24/7 service and emergency restoration to their largest and most complex projects. Our proven safety record, technical depth, and longstanding client relationships have made us a partner of choice for Fortune 500 companies, leading general contractors, and EPC contractors. 
We are seeking a **DIRECTOR OF FABRICATION** to support our Mission Critical team. 
 
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Champion Safety Culture.** Set the standard through visible, consistent leadership. Ensure fabrication, material handling, equipment operation, and facility activities are planned and performed in alignment with company requirements and applicable safety standards.
* **Lead from the Facility Floor.** This is a working leadership role. Maintain a consistent presence in the facility, understand the daily heartbeat of the operation, engage the team directly, and act quickly when conditions require attention.
* **Facility Operations and Execution.** Lead the day-to-day operation of an 80,000 square-foot fabrication facility, including fabrication, modular assembly, receiving, inventory, shipping, equipment, maintenance, and facility services.
* **Production Planning.** Translate the demand and released work scopes of multiple regional projects into practical weekly and monthly production plans. Align labor, materials, equipment, floor space, and support resources with field installation sequence and committed delivery dates.
* **Reliable Flow and Delivery.** Monitor backlog, throughput, labor performance, work in process, capacity, and on-time completion. Balance work across production areas, remove constraints, and communicate risks before they become missed commitments.
* **Field First Fabrication and DFMI.** Partner with preconstruction, planning, modeling, procurement, operations, and field leadership to turn coordinated information into fabrication ready work. Help advance repeatable assemblies, kitting, bills of material, and installation-ready work packages.
* **Quality and Standards.** Establish practical inspection, testing, release, and nonconformance processes that protect workmanship, accuracy, traceability, and project requirements. Maintain standards with discipline while remaining agile when project or market conditions require a different path.
* **Inventory, Warehousing, and Logistics.** Maintain material visibility and inventory accuracy from receipt through shipment. Improve packaging, loading, transportation, delivery tracking, and site handoff while reducing shortages, damage, excess inventory, obsolete material, and double handling.
* **Financial and Operational Stewardship.** Manage the facility operating budget and the cost drivers within the role, including labor, equipment, maintenance, occupancy, material handling, logistics, and overhead. Provide forecasts and clear explanations of material variances.
* **Build and Develop the Team.** Recruit, organize, coach, and retain production and support personnel. Set clear accountabilities, staffing and training plans, and performance expectations while building a culture of safety, respect, urgency, craftsmanship, teamwork, and ownership.
* **Continuous Improvement.** Apply practical Lean methods, standardized work, visual management, and structured problem solving. Improve flow, first pass quality, cycle time, productivity, and usable capacity without creating process for the sake of process.

The OPM & NPI Lead serves as the primary operational leader responsible for the successful execution of both sustaining programs and New Product Introduction (NPI) initiatives. This role provides leadership for a team of Operations Product Managers while ensuring operational readiness, production launch success, customer commitment attainment, and portfolio performance. Acting as the operational integrator between General Management, Program Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, and SIOP functions, the OPM & NPI Lead drives execution across the entire product lifecycle. The role ensures new products transition effectively from development into production while maintaining delivery, cost, quality, inventory, and capacity objectives for existing programs.

Must be willing and able to travel 15% of the time.

**What You Will Do:**

*Portfolio Leadership*

* Provide operations leadership within Program Management Teams
* Lead and develop a team of Operations Product Managers
* Establish priorities and allocate resources across product portfolios
* Ensure alignment of customer commitments with manufacturing capacity
* Lead portfolio reviews and executive status reporting
* Support business growth initiatives and strategic program execution
* Develop business cases supporting investments and growth opportunities

*New Product Introduction (NPI)*

* Lead operational execution of NPI programs from concept through production stabilization
* Conduct manufacturing feasibility and producibility assessments
* Ensure readiness of labor, equipment, tooling, facilities, materials, and processes
* Lead launch readiness reviews and milestone assessments
* Manage transition from development to recurring production
* Manufacturing Operations Leadership
* Translate forecasted demand into executable manufacturing plans
* Lead recovery efforts for missed deliveries and production disruptions
* Develop capacity models and identify future resource requirements
* Manage operational risks and mitigation strategies

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Typically requires a University Degree and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience **or**an Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years of experience
* 5+ years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing, operations, program management, or NPI leadership
* 5+ years of leadership experience with direct reports
* Experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex manufacturing environment
* 3+ years experience managing new product introductions and production transitions
* Understanding of SIOP, capacity planning, production control, and operational performance metrics

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, Su
